title: Beef Bourguignon
subtitle: Slow-braised beef with mushrooms and bacon
excerpt: Beef bourguignon is a two-and-a-half hour project that rewards patience. Chuck beef has enough collagen to turn silky in a slow braise, and the sauce thickens naturally as it reduces. This version uses beef stock where the recipe would traditionally use red wine.
sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is the canonical Burgundian braise, made famous internationally by Julia Child's version in Mastering the Art of French Cooking. The dish is traditionally cooked in red Burgundy wine, which gives the sauce its depth and colour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the finished stew for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Makes excellent batch-cook portions. Double the recipe in a larger pot for the same cook time.

content.text: Do not skip browning the beef in small batches. Each batch needs space to develop a dark crust -- this is where most of the flavour in the finished sauce comes from. Pat the beef dry before it goes in the pan. This recipe uses beef stock in place of the traditional red Burgundy wine; the result is a lighter colour but the same tender, deeply savoury braise.

Pat the beef dry and season generously. Heat the olive oil in the stockpot over high heat. Brown the beef in batches of 5-6 pieces, turning until deeply coloured on all sides. Remove each batch and set aside.
Add the pancetta to the pot and cook for 4 minutes until the fat has rendered. Add the onion and carrot and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the beef stock, scraping up any browned bits. Add the bay leaves, thyme, and the browned beef. The liquid should come about two-thirds up the meat. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 2 hours, stirring every 30 minutes. The beef is ready when it yields easily to a spoon but has not fallen apart.
Add the mushrooms for the last 20 minutes of cooking, leaving the lid off. Stir in the butter off the heat. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning.

items.cause: Heat too low or pieces too large.
items.fix: Check the braise is at a gentle simmer -- not just warm. Cut any remaining large pieces in half and cook for another 30 minutes.

items.cause: Lid kept on throughout, preventing reduction.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes of cooking and let the liquid reduce until it coats the back of a spoon.
